title: Use a master detail rail for repeat visits
intent: Let a returning user reach any object in one click without losing their place.
when_to_use: the user picks one object from a set of many similar objects and works inside it
the same screen is opened many times a day by the same person
the selection must be linkable so it can be shared or reopened
when_not_to_use: the objects are compared across several shared columns, where the table is the right family
the set is under five items, where inline expansion is cheaper than a rail
the detail view is a long document read once, where the rail steals reading width
rules: the list is persistent and is never replaced by a modal or a route change
the selected row is identifiable at rest, without hover, by at least two signals
the selected object appears in the URL so the view can be reopened or shared
the rail width is fixed at every breakpoint below the layout switch, and the detail pane never reflows it
no decorative status dot carries meaning; a status is a word plus, where useful, a shape
trade_off: You give up the full canvas of a list page and the freedom to give each object its own view, because a persistent rail constrains every detail layout to the same width.
failure_mode: The rail becomes a second navigation layer: nested lists inside the list, a detail pane that scrolls inside a page that also scrolls, and a selection state visible only on hover.

example.brief: Support inbox where an agent handles dozens of conversations a day.
example.ruling: Shell family master-detail-rail: fixed 320px conversation list on the leading edge, selected thread in the URL, detail pane on the trailing side. Status is a word in the row, not a coloured dot.
